scope: Use the published ALGAL task API for existing Textbutler habitat inference and expose a bounded read-only view of its existing evaluation operations.

dependency.name: @hraness/algal
dependency.validation: Installed from the published Git commit with Bun 1.3.14; package.json and bun.lock agree. The focused suite below imports that installed artifact without local source mappings. Other dependency pins are unchanged.

independentReview.reviewer: Cloud implementation worker (separate agent from the Textbutler implementer)
independentReview.method: Read-only review of the runtime, test, cost-registry and documentation changes against the base commit. No tests repeated by the reviewer. This source review preceded the final dependency installation; dependency verification is recorded separately.
independentReview.result: No blocking finding in the reviewed changes.
findings: `habitat-program.ts`: phase instructions and memory instructions are unchanged. The compiler preserves the prompt when no demonstrations are supplied. Context still passes through the same `{ evidence, preferences }` value; object-only output, one model call, four steps, 200,000 work, 16 KiB effect output and phase deadlines are preserved. Raising the explicit reflection/judge run context ceiling accommodates the existing 106,496-byte cell override rather than raising the effective model context limit. The 65,536-byte run output limit and depth four preserve prior defaults. The cell ID changes from `model` to `task`, so new manifests/receipts receive new identities; retained evidence includes its original manifest.

Provider ownership remains with the host. Its executor wrapper still removes retry/cache authority, combines the external and runtime abort signals, checks cancellation after provider settlement and tracks the provider promise. The new `finally` joins that promise even when the task runner fails. It introduces no send capability or uncertain-result retry. As before, a provider that never settles can hold cleanup open; the change does not claim process-kill recovery.

`inspectHabitatOperations` derives at most 80 rows from validated retained state and current contact-scoped runner liveness. A missing live owner marks a claimed pending checkpoint uncertain, does not return it to the queue, and keeps cancellation unknown. Requested cancellation is shown only while the matching active signal is aborted. Retained/promoted outcomes describe plan decisions, not external completion guarantees. All rows say `repeatable: false`.

The operation callback is read-only and unregisters after runner cleanup. Single existing evolution ownership bounds the active callback; no parallel evaluation scheduling or lifecycle authority was added.

Control responses retain the existing 256 KiB bound and increment omission counters when trimming. New rows add keys, phases, reason strings and receipt identities; they do not add conversation bodies. Existing reason strings and learned memory remain within the same authenticated local habitat view. Durable state schema, credential handling, send policy and promotion restrictions are unchanged.

focusedValidation.logRetention: The integration owner retains the complete system-one check log, also copied to the local research evidence directory.
coverage: Phase-specific context, output, work, model-call and deadline limits; object output contract and generic replay.
Provider cleanup after cancellation, failed-result nonretryability and no additional effect authority.
Unknown pending claims, current-runner cancellation visibility, receipt identities, response bounds and no read-side journal writes.
Existing contact habitat, control-service and reply-loop regressions.

aggregateValidation.note: This record binds the actual focused source and dependency evidence. It does not claim the final aggregate, distribution build, CI or deployment has passed.

limitations: New task manifests use the task agent cell name in place of model, so new manifest and receipt identities differ; retained evidence preserves its original manifest.
The existing provider owns cleanup. A provider that never settles can hold cleanup open; cancellation request does not prove remote completion.
No live provider call, account activation, messaging, production qualification or deployment was performed for this evidence.
